entries.summary: The most expensive KV cache in this catalogue by a wide margin. All 92 layers use full attention with no sliding window and no linear-attention layers, giving 368KB per token — so a 32K context costs 12GB of cache before a single weight is loaded, and filling the 198K window would cost about 71GB. On a machine sized to just hold the weights, context is what you run out of first.

mitigations.note: Architectural. Budget the cache explicitly: the RUNS AT line on this site prices it at the context you pick.

entries.summary: For almost everyone this model is only reachable at 2-3 bit — the 4-bit build is 205GB and the bf16 weights are 717GB. Unsloth's dynamic 2-bit lands around 135GB, which is the first size that fits a single large machine. That is a real option, but it is the bottom of the quant ladder, and expert routing in a 358B MoE is exactly what degrades there.

mitigations.note: Move up to the 205GB 4-bit build if you have the memory; the gap between 2-bit and 4-bit is larger here than on a small dense model.
